title: General Last-k-Digits Theorem
content:
The master theorem for all last-digit rules:

```lean
theorem dvd_iff_dvd_mod (d M n : ℕ) (hdM : d ∣ M) :
    d ∣ n ↔ d ∣ (n % M)
```

If $d | M$, then $d | n \iff d | (n \bmod M)$. This unifies:
- div by 2 (M=10): 2|10
- div by 4 (M=100): 4|100
- div by 8 (M=1000): 8|1000
- div by 5, 25, 125 similarly
prerequisites: modular arithmetic and congruences mod m

title: Power Generalizations
content:
General theorems for all powers of 2 and 5:

```lean
theorem pow2_dvd_last_k (k n : ℕ) :
    2^k ∣ n ↔ 2^k ∣ (n % 10^k)
theorem pow5_dvd_last_k (k n : ℕ) :
    5^k ∣ n ↔ 5^k ∣ (n % 10^k)
```

These subsume all individual 2/4/8/16/32 and 5/25/125 rules.
prerequisites: divisibility tests by the last k digits
powers of 2 and 5 as factors of 10^k

title: Divisibility by 13: Truncation Method
content:
The 'add 4 times the last digit' rule for 13:

```lean
theorem thirteen_dvd_truncation (n : ℕ) :
    13 ∣ n ↔ (13 : ℤ) ∣ (↑(n/10) + 4·↑(n%10))
```

**Proof idea**: $10(q + 4r) = n + 39r \equiv n \pmod{13}$, and $\gcd(13, 10) = 1$.

This gives a practical mental test: remove last digit, add 4 times it to the rest.
prerequisites: the truncation/seed step for divisibility by primes coprime to 10

title: Digit-Sum Rules in Various Bases
content:
General digit-sum divisibility via Mathlib:

```lean
theorem digitSum_dvd_iff (d b : ℕ) (hdb : b % d = 1) (n : ℕ) :
    d ∣ n ↔ d ∣ (Nat.digits b n).sum
```

Instantiations include:
- 37 via base 1000 (three-digit grouping)
- 99 via base 100 (two-digit grouping)
- 27, 999 via base 1000
- Rules in hex (3, 5, 15), octal (7), and base 7 (3, 6)
mathContext: $b \equiv 1 \pmod{d} \implies (d | n \iff d | \text{digit sum in base } b)$
prerequisites: the congruence b ≡ 1 (mod m) underlying digit-sum rules

title: Casting Out Nines and Threes
content:
Digit sums preserve arithmetic modulo 9 and 3:

```lean
theorem casting_out_nines_add (a b : ℕ) :
    (a + b) ≡ (digitSum(a) + digitSum(b)) [MOD 9]
theorem casting_out_nines_mul (a b : ℕ) :
    (a * b) ≡ (digitSum(a) * digitSum(b)) [MOD 9]
```

This formalizes the ancient technique of checking arithmetic by casting out nines.
mathContext: Digit sums are ring homomorphisms mod 9

title: Digital Root Theory
content:
Complete formalization of digital roots:

```lean
def digitalRoot (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0
  else if n % 9 = 0 then 9 else n % 9
```

Key properties:
- Always ≤ 9, positive for n > 0
- dr(n) = 9 ↔ 9 | n (for n > 0)
- 3 | n ↔ 3 | dr(n)
- dr(n) % 3 = n % 3
prerequisites: the digit-sum rule and iterated digit sums

title: Coprime Factorization Rules
content:
General coprime divisibility and 8 specific rules:

```lean
theorem coprime_mul_dvd_iff (d₁ d₂ n : ℕ) (h : Nat.Coprime d₁ d₂) :
    d₁ * d₂ ∣ n ↔ d₁ ∣ n ∧ d₂ ∣ n
```

Rules: 6=2×3, 12=4×3, 15=3×5, 18=2×9, 36=4×9, 45=9×5, 60=4×15, 90=9×10.
mathContext: $\gcd(d_1, d_2) = 1 \implies (d_1 d_2 | n \iff d_1 | n \wedge d_2 | n)$
prerequisites: the CRT principle: m·n | x iff m|x and n|x for coprime m,n

title: Master Summary
content:
A single theorem collecting all major divisibility rules:

- 3 digit-sum rules (3, 9, 37, 99 in various bases)
- 5 last-digit rules (2, 4, 8, 5, 25)
- 2 power generalizations (2^k, 5^k)

All verified in one theorem statement.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of master summary
prerequisites: the individual divisibility rules (last-k-digits, digit-sum, truncation)
